details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:120-135 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `validation_ok=true` and related success outputs are written before the copy loop completes, so a later `cp` failure leaves the step reporting success despite failing.
  WHY: All reviewers identified the same pre-mutation output timing bug; this can mislead downstream consumers after a failed update.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:93-96 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `::error::${code}: ${detail_sanitized}` annotation is not fully escaped for GitHub Actions command parsing, so special characters in the detail text can break the annotation.
  WHY: Reviewers agreed the sanitization is incomplete; severity differs only in emphasis, so the highest reported severity is kept.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:144,160 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `cp` operations lack explicit failure handling, so copy failures exit generically without recording a categorized failure reason.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers flagged the same missing error-handling path around the copy commands.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:131,144,164 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `SKIPPED_FILES` is accumulated and written to `/tmp/skipped_files.txt`, but the summary step never reports it.
  WHY: Reviewers consistently noted the skipped-file information is tracked but omitted from the job summary.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:125-230 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py` is not executed by CI.
  WHY: All reviewers agreed the new guardrail test is unregistered, so regressions in the workflow safety checks will not be caught.
- tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:1-99 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The test file uses tab indentation instead of spaces.
  WHY: Reviewers consistently reported the indentation style issue; reported confidence varies, so the highest confidence is kept.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:107 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The workflow hardcodes the upstream self-template filename `ai-update-workflows.yml`, making validation brittle if the upstream naming changes.
  WHY: This is the same upstream-path assumption reported by multiple reviewers and would block updates if the template name changes.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:264-348 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The summary step’s outcome handling is not robust across empty or skipped state combinations.
  WHY: Reviewers described the same incomplete categorical handling; the issue is less concrete than the others, so the lower confidence is preserved.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:120-135 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `validation_ok=true` is set after pre-mutation validation passes but before the actual copy (`cp`) operations. If a copy fails, the step outputs will indicate `validation_ok=true` while the step actually failed.
  WHY: Downstream consumers checking `validation_ok` will get misleading success signals even when the update step failed during file copying.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:93-96 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The GitHub error annotation `::error::${code}: ${detail_sanitized}` doesn't escape special annotation characters in the detail text.
  WHY: If `detail_sanitized` contains `:` or `]`, GitHub Actions may parse the annotation incorrectly, causing malformed error display or parse failures.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:144, 160 (and similar cp commands) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `cp "$upstream_file" "$local_file"` commands lack error handling and don't provide categorized failure reasons.
  WHY: Copy failures (disk full, permissions, missing source) exit with generic shell error instead of actionable `ERR_FILE_COPY_FAILED` reason.
- tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:1-76 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The test file uses tab indentation instead of spaces.
  WHY: Violates PEP 8; Python tools expecting space indentation may warn or fail. Mixed indentation could cause `TabError`.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:Not in file | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The new guardrail test `test_update_workflows_guardrails.py` is not executed by CI.
  WHY: Regressions in the update_workflows guardrails won't be detected automatically.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:107 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The workflow hardcodes assumption that `ai-update-workflows.yml` exists in upstream `workflow-templates/`.
  WHY: If upstream template naming/path changes, validation will always fail, blocking all updates.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:131, 144, 164 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `SKIPPED_FILES` is accumulated and written to `/tmp/skipped_files.txt` but never included in the summary output.
  WHY: Users won't see which files were skipped (self-updater) in the workflow summary, losing visibility.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:264-334 (Summary section) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The summary step handles some empty outcome variables with defaults but doesn't cover all categorical status combinations robustly.
  WHY: If early steps are skipped or fail in unexpected ways, outcome variables may be empty/inconsistent, leading to incorrect summary behavior.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:120-135 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The writability check loop iterates through all templates, but if a later template fails the writability check, earlier output variables already set `validation_ok=true`.
  WHY: Inconsistent state - validation passes initial checks, sets `validation_ok=true`, but then fails on a later file's writability check.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:fail_with_reason function | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The function uses `local detail_sanitized="${detail//$'\r'/ }"` which only replaces carriage returns with spaces, not removing other control characters.
  WHY: Control characters in error details could break output formatting or cause parsing issues.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:164 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `printf '%s' "$SKIPPED_FILES" > /tmp/skipped_files.txt` - if `$SKIPPED_FILES` is empty, creates an empty file rather than no file.
  WHY: The summary step checks `if [ -f "${FAILURE_REASON_FILE}" ]` but assumes file existence implies non-empty content, which may not be true for skipped files.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:94 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The error annotation message uses a raw variable `${code}: ${detail_sanitized}` without escaping characters that have special meaning in GitHub Actions workflow commands (like `:`, `]`).
  WHY: If the detail message contains these characters, the workflow command parser may misinterpret the line, leading to malformed annotations or silent failure of the error report in the UI.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:121, 134-136 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Step output variables (`templates_checked`, `templates_updated`, `templates_created`, `has_updates`) are set to their final cumulative values *before* the actual file modification loop (`cp`) starts.
  WHY: If a `cp` command fails (e.g., due to disk space or transient I/O error) after some files have been updated, the step will exit with an error, but the `Summary` job (which uses `if: always()`) will read these output variables and report them as if those counts were successfully applied to the workspace.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:144, 160 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `cp` commands are not wrapped in safety checks or failure markers (like the `fail_with_reason` helper used earlier).
  WHY: A `cp` failure results in a generic shell exit code 1. The `Summary` step's logic for `UPDATE_OUTCOME = "failure"` will then fall through to the "ERR_UNCATEGORIZED_FAILURE" branch because no specific failure code was written to state, making it harder to diagnose why the update failed.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:141 (within the loop) | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The code accumulates `SKIPPED_FILES` but never writes it to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` or a file that the `Summary` step can read.
  WHY: The information about which files were skipped (specifically the self-updater sentinel) is lost and not displayed in the Job Summary, even though updated/created files are.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:125-230 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The new test file `tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py` is not registered in the `CI` workflow.
  WHY: Regressions in the update workflow's safety guardrails (which the PR description specifically claims to add) will not be detected by CI, allowing breaking changes to land on main.
- tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:14, 21, 42, 59 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The file uses literal tab characters for indentation (visible in raw diff as `\t` behavior).
  WHY: While functionally correct in Python, it violates the repository's preference for spaces in Python (checked by `ruff` and standard PEP 8 practices) and may trigger linting failures or `TabError` if future edits by other tools mix in spaces.

=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.ql:120, 136, 150 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `validation_ok=true` is set before the copy operations that can fail.
  WHY: If a copy operation fails after the validation outputs are set, downstream consumers will see `validation_ok=true` even though the step actually failed.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.ql:91-99 (fail_with_reason function) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The function sanitizes only `\r` and `\n` but doesn't escape GitHub Actions annotation-sensitive characters like `::`, `[`, `]`, or `,`.
  WHY: Special characters in error messages can cause malformed annotations or incorrect UI rendering in GitHub Actions.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.ql:136, 150 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `cp` commands are executed without error handling that would record a categorized failure reason.
  WHY: Users receive generic command failures instead of specific actionable error codes like `ERR_FILE_COPY_FAILED`.
- tests/test_update_workspace_workflows_guardrails.ql:1-99 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test file uses tab characters for indentation, violating PEP 8 Python style guidelines.
  WHY: Can trigger formatting warnings or cause issues if mixed with space-based indentation in the same file.
- .github/workflows/ci.ql: | severit
